title: 40. Influence of weaning strategy, pulmonary arterial pressure, and performance outcomes in beef heifers.
content:
Abstract
Bovine congestive heart failure threatens beef production and may be influenced by weaning stress and respiratory disease. We evaluated the effects of weaning strategy and preconditioning on backgrounding performance and pulmonary arterial pressure (PAP) in beef heifers. Calves from the University of Wyoming were assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design, stratified by age of dam (AOD) and assigned to one of four treatments: no preconditioning with immediate weaning (NoPC+IW; n = 11), preconditioning with immediate weaning (PC+IW; n = 14), no preconditioning with fenceline weaning (NoPC+FW; n = 13), or preconditioning with fenceline weaning (PC+FW; n = 14). Heifers received respiratory and clostridial vaccines 45 d prior to weaning (PC only) and at weaning (d 0; PC and NoPC). PAP was measured at d 0, 18, 35, 84, 211, and 325. A feed efficiency trial was conducted from d 20 to 84, where individual intake was monitored using the Vytelle SENSE system and body weights were collected biweekly. Performance variables included dry matter intake (DMI), average daily gain (ADG), residual feed intake (RFI), feed conversion ratio (FCR), and gain-to-feed (G:F). Following backgrounding, heifers were managed under standard herd practices. PAP data were logit-transformed to evaluate temporal changes over time. To assess the temporal aspect of PAP, data were first transformed with a logit transformation then change in transformed PAP was calculated for d 0 vs. 84 (deltaAD), d 0 vs. 211 (deltaAE), d 84 vs. 211 (delta DE), and d 211 vs. 325 (deltaEF). These change in PAP data were analyzed using the Reg procedure of SAS (v.9.04) with initial transformed PAP in the comparison, weaning and preconditioning treatment as predictors along with birth weight (BW), weaning weight (WW), age of dam (AOD), and feed efficiency metrics. The model was significant for deltaAD, (P < 0.0001, R² = 0.56) where transformed PAP at d 0 (-0.73; P = 0.0051), WW (-0.21; P < 0.0001), RFI (-2.54; P < 0.0001) and DMI (1.57; P = 0.018) were significant predictors. The model was significant for deltaAE (P < 0.04; R2 =0.32) with the only significant predictor as AOD (-0.18; P = 0.02). The model for deltaDE was significant (P < 0.001; R2 = 0.46) where transformed PAP at d 84 (-0.91; P < 0.0001) and AOD (-0.22; P = 0.001) were significant predictors. Finally, the model for deltaEF was significant (P < 0.0001; R2 = 0.77) where transformed PAP at d 211 (-0.64; P < 0.0001), RFI (-1.18; P = 0.04), BW (0.03; P < 0.005), and WW (0.03; P = 0.006) were significant predictors. Over time, these data indicate PAP is largely influenced by age of calf at birth and weaning, age of dam, and partially to feed efficiency rather than weaning management.
